phc.op.abha-link.description:
An ABHA is the patient's national health number. Linking one to their record
here is how a hospital in another district finds their history later.
phc.op.abha-link.summary: Connect this patient's record to their national health account so their records can be found elsewhere later.
phc.op.abha-link.title: Create or link an ABHA for this patient

phc.op.consult-document.description:
The doctor's note. This is narrative, and narrative is the one thing ambient
capture is genuinely good at, because context recovers a dropped word and the
clinician catches the rest on review.
phc.op.consult-document.summary: Write down what the patient said, what was found, and what the doctor concluded.
phc.op.consult-document.title: Document a consultation

phc.op.household-visit.description:
An accredited social health activist or auxiliary nurse midwife visits a
household and records the visit. This is the community half of the system and
the half that CARE was not built for, so it is ours to design.
phc.op.household-visit.summary: A frontline worker records what happened at a visit to someone's home, and anything that needs following up.
phc.op.household-visit.title: Record a household visit

phc.op.lab-order.description: The doctor asks for a test. The request lands on the lab's worklist.
phc.op.lab-order.summary: Ask the laboratory to run a test for this patient.
phc.op.lab-order.title: Order an investigation

phc.op.lab-result-enter.description:
The lab technician types in what the test measured. This is a number, and a
number entered wrongly here is acted on at district review months later
without anybody noticing it was ever wrong.
phc.op.lab-result-enter.summary: Record the value a bench test produced, against the investigation a doctor ordered for this patient.
phc.op.lab-result-enter.title: Enter a laboratory result

phc.op.patient-register.description:
Make a new patient record. This is the second thing the clerk does, never the
first. The first thing is always to search.
phc.op.patient-register.summary: Create a record for someone the facility has not seen before, after searching and finding nobody who matches.
phc.op.patient-register.title: Register a new patient

phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.description:
The pharmacist hands over medicine and records it. What gets recorded is what
the patient was actually given, which is not always what the doctor wrote.
Stockouts at a primary health centre are routine, so a partial dispense is a
normal outcome and not an error.
phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.summary: Give the patient the medicines a doctor prescribed, record what they actually received, and take that quantity out of facility stock.
phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.title: Dispense against a confirmed prescription

phc.op.rx-prescribe.description:
The doctor prescribes. Confirming the prescription is what makes the
pharmacist's dispense action exist at all.
phc.op.rx-prescribe.summary: Prescribe medicines for this patient, with what the pharmacy actually has in view.
phc.op.rx-prescribe.title: Write a prescription

phc.op.vitals-record.description:
The nurse takes the patient's readings and records them. These are numbers,
and they travel: an abnormal blood pressure recorded here becomes a district
level statistic and a treatment decision.
phc.op.vitals-record.summary: Measure and record blood pressure, oxygen saturation, weight and the other basic readings, and flag anything abnormal for the doctor.
phc.op.vitals-record.title: Record vitals and triage
